title: Incomplete Conquest of Canaan
summary: After Joshua's death, Judah and Simeon defeat Adoni-bezek and capture cities in the hill country, Othniel wins Achsah in marriage, but Benjamin, Manasseh, and the other tribes fail to drive out the Canaanites from their territory.
blurb: Judah conquers south Canaan; other tribes fail

title: The Angel's Rebuke and Joshua's Death
summary: An angel confronts Israel at Bochim for failing to break down pagan altars, Joshua dies at a hundred and ten, and a new generation arises that does not know the LORD or his works.
blurb: The angel's rebuke at Bochim; Joshua's death

title: Othniel, Ehud, and Shamgar
summary: The LORD leaves nations in Canaan to test Israel; Othniel defeats Cushan-rishathaim, Ehud assassinates the Moabite king Eglon and routs his army at the Jordan, and Shamgar kills six hundred Philistines with an oxgoad.
blurb: Othniel, Ehud's assassination of Eglon, and Shamgar

title: Deborah and Barak Defeat Sisera
summary: Deborah summons Barak to fight Sisera's nine hundred chariots at Mount Tabor, the LORD routs the Canaanite army by the Kishon River, and Jael kills the fleeing Sisera with a tent peg in her tent.
blurb: Jael kills Sisera with a tent peg

title: The Song of Deborah
summary: Deborah and Barak celebrate the victory over Sisera in song, praising the tribes who fought and cursing Meroz for staying home, and picturing Sisera's mother waiting anxiously at her window for a son who will not return.
blurb: Deborah and Barak's victory song

title: Gideon's Call and the Fleece
summary: Midian's raids drive Israel into hiding until the angel of the LORD calls the fearful Gideon to save Israel; Gideon tears down his father's altar to Baal by night and tests the LORD twice with a wool fleece.
blurb: Gideon's call and the fleece test

title: Gideon's Three Hundred
summary: The LORD narrows Gideon's army to three hundred men by a water test, Gideon overhears a Midianite's dream of a barley loaf, and the three hundred rout Midian's camp at night with trumpets, jars, and torches.
blurb: Three hundred men rout Midian by night

title: Gideon's Victory and Refusal to Rule
summary: Gideon pursues and captures the Midianite kings Zebah and Zalmunna, punishing Succoth and Penuel for refusing his men bread, executes the kings, and refuses Israel's offer to make him king, though his golden ephod later becomes a snare.
blurb: Gideon refuses to be king

title: Abimelech's Kingship and Death
summary: Abimelech murders his seventy brothers and is made king at Shechem; Jotham curses him with a fable of the trees, Gaal's revolt leads Abimelech to destroy Shechem, and Abimelech dies at Thebez when a woman drops a millstone on his head.
blurb: Abimelech's murder of his brothers and death

title: Tola, Jair, and Israel's Idolatry
summary: Tola and Jair judge Israel for a combined forty-five years; Israel then worships foreign gods, and the LORD hands them over to the Ammonites and Philistines until their cry for help moves him to relent.
blurb: Tola and Jair judge Israel

title: Jephthah's Vow
summary: Gilead's outcast son Jephthah is recruited to lead Israel against Ammon, vows to sacrifice whatever meets him at his door if he wins, defeats the Ammonites, and is met by his only daughter, whom he then sacrifices.
blurb: Jephthah's vow costs his daughter's life

title: Ephraim's Revolt and the Shibboleth
summary: Ephraim threatens Jephthah for excluding them from the battle against Ammon, Gilead defeats Ephraim and catches fleeing survivors at the Jordan with the password Shibboleth, and Ibzan, Elon, and Abdon judge Israel in turn.
blurb: The Shibboleth test at the Jordan

title: The Angel Announces Samson's Birth
summary: An angel tells the barren wife of Manoah that she will bear a Nazirite son who will begin delivering Israel from the Philistines, and after the angel ascends in the flame of their offering, Samson is born.
blurb: The angel announces Samson's birth

title: Samson's Riddle at Timnah
summary: Samson insists on marrying a Philistine woman from Timnah, kills a lion barehanded and later eats honey from its carcass, and loses a riddle wager at his wedding feast after his wife pries out the answer.
blurb: Samson's riddle and the lion's honey

title: Samson's Revenge on the Philistines
summary: After his wife is given to another man, Samson burns Philistine fields with three hundred foxes, kills a thousand men with a donkey's jawbone after Judah hands him over, and drinks water the LORD provides at Lehi.
blurb: Samson kills a thousand with a jawbone

title: Samson and Delilah
summary: Samson tears down Gaza's city gate, Delilah wears him down until he reveals that his strength lies in his uncut Nazirite hair, and after the Philistines blind him he pulls down the temple of Dagon in his death.
blurb: Samson pulls down the temple of Dagon

title: Micah's Household Shrine
summary: Micah's mother dedicates silver he stole from her to make idols for a household shrine, and a wandering Levite from Bethlehem agrees to serve as Micah's priest, since Israel has no king to keep it from doing as it pleases.
blurb: Micah hires a Levite as his priest

title: The Danites Take Micah's Idols
summary: Danite spies find Micah's shrine and are told their journey is blessed; six hundred armed Danites take his idols and his priest for themselves, then conquer the peaceful city of Laish and rename it Dan.
blurb: Dan steals Micah's idols and conquers Laish

title: The Levite's Concubine at Gibeah
summary: A Levite retrieves his concubine from Bethlehem, but the men of Gibeah surround the house where they lodge for the night and abuse her until she dies, and he cuts her body into twelve pieces to send throughout Israel.
blurb: Gibeah's crime against the Levite's concubine

title: Israel's War Against Benjamin
summary: Israel assembles to hear the Levite's account and demands Gibeah's guilty men, but Benjamin refuses and wins two battles before Israel ambushes and burns Gibeah, killing all but six hundred men of Benjamin.
blurb: Israel nearly wipes out the tribe of Benjamin

title: Wives for Benjamin
summary: Israel regrets its oath never to give Benjamin wives, destroys Jabesh-gilead for skipping the assembly and spares its virgins for Benjamin, and lets the tribe's last survivors seize wives from among the dancers at Shiloh's festival.
blurb: Benjamin's survivors find wives at Shiloh
